name: Asthma data (download)
description: A downloadable file of asthma emergency department visits and hospital stays among Colorado residents, by county. It's the data behind the asthma dashboard on the Colorado Environmental Public Health Tracking site.
population: Colorado residents

name: Baby & You Survey
description: A series of four online surveys for birthing parents of children ages 0-3. CDPHE samples postpartum people each month from live birth certificates and invites them to enroll at 3-4 months postpartum, then follows up around the baby's first, second, and third birthdays. The sample intentionally oversamples American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian American/Pacific Islander, and Black/African American birthing people. Results are weighted to represent all births in Colorado. Weighted data tables are published by birth cohort, and custom estimates or de-identified datasets can be requested from the program.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Birthing parents of children ages 0-3

name: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System
description: An ongoing, federally funded statewide random telephone survey of Colorado adults ages 18 and older, with 12,000 to 15,000 respondents a year. It tracks how common health behaviors, chronic and infectious conditions, and preventive health practices are, and what drives the leading causes of chronic disease, infectious disease, drug use, disability, injury, and death. Annual summary tables and questionnaires are published for each survey year. Results are also shown in the VISION chronic disease dashboard.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Adults 18+

name: Carbon monoxide poisoning data (download)
description: A downloadable file of carbon monoxide poisoning among Colorado residents: emergency department visits, hospital stays and deaths. It's the data behind the carbon monoxide dashboard on the Colorado Environmental Public Health Tracking site.
population: Colorado residents

name: Childhood lead poisoning data (download)
description: A downloadable spreadsheet of blood lead testing among Colorado children, by county. It's the data behind the childhood lead poisoning dashboard on the Colorado Environmental Public Health Tracking site. A data dictionary explains each field.
population: Children and teens under 19 in Colorado

name: Colorado Autism and Developmental Disabilities Monitoring
description: Tracks autism spectrum disorder among children in the seven-county Denver metro area: Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas and Jefferson counties. You can only see the data in short snapshot reports. The most recent public report covers 2016.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: Children in the seven-county Denver metro area

name: Colorado Basic Screening Survey data (download)
description: A downloadable spreadsheet of results from the Colorado Basic Screening Survey (BSS), a dental check of kindergarten and third-grade students at school. It covers five school years from 2003–04 to 2022–23, statewide, with breakdowns by race and ethnicity, school free or reduced-price lunch level, and urban or rural location.
population: Kindergarten and third-grade students

name: Colorado Central Cancer Registry
description: The statewide registry of cancer diagnoses among Colorado residents. Cases are reported by hospitals, pathology labs, other state registries, death certificates, and some physicians. Records include cancer site, stage at diagnosis, treatment, payer, and demographics such as age, sex, race, and residence, covering about 25,000 invasive cases a year. Aggregate incidence data are available through CoHID dashboards. Custom data requests and de-identified research datasets are available on approval. New data are usually complete 18 to 24 months after the end of the year.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents diagnosed with cancer, all ages

name: Colorado End-of-Life Options Act reporting
description: Reports that doctors and pharmacists must send to CDPHE when they prescribe or dispense medical aid-in-dying medication under Colorado's End-of-Life Options Act, matched to death certificates. The individual reports are confidential. You can only see the data in CDPHE's yearly summary reports.
population: Terminally ill patients prescribed aid-in-dying medication in Colorado

name: Colorado foodborne illness data
description: Counts and rates of illnesses that people in Colorado got from food, such as botulism and cholera. You can only see the data in yearly PDF tables for 2014 to 2017, broken down by disease, age group, sex, and race and ethnicity.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: People in Colorado with a reported foodborne illness

name: Colorado reportable disease dataset, 2016–2025
description: A downloadable file of yearly case counts and rates for diseases that doctors and labs must report to the state. It is the same data shown in the reportable disease dashboard. Sexually transmitted infections, hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis and lead are tracked separately and are not included.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Colorado residents

name: Colorado STI and HIV surveillance
description: Cases of HIV and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) such as chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis that doctors and labs must report to CDPHE. You can see the data in the HIV and STI dashboards and in yearly and quarterly reports. More detailed data are only available by request.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: People diagnosed with HIV or an STI in Colorado

name: Colorado tuberculosis data
description: Tuberculosis (TB) case data from CDPHE's TB program. You can download county case tables and yearly reports. Record-level data are not available.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: People diagnosed with TB in Colorado

name: Colorado Violent Death Reporting System
description: Detailed information on suicides, homicides, unintentional firearm deaths and other violent deaths in Colorado. It combines death certificates, coroner and medical examiner reports, and law enforcement records. You can see the data in the suicide and homicide dashboards and in HealthWatch reports. Other data are only available by request.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Violent deaths in Colorado

name: Colorado vital statistics
description: Official counts of births, deaths, fetal deaths, abortions, marriages and divorces in Colorado. You can see the data in the birth and death dashboards and in downloadable summary tables. More detailed data are only available by request.
population: Births, deaths and other vital events in Colorado

name: Colorado WIC program data
description: Data from Colorado's Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). WIC provides healthy food, nutrition advice and referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants and young children. You can see the data in a dashboard and in yearly reports. Data with personal details are not shared.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: WIC participants in Colorado

name: COPD data (download)
description: A downloadable spreadsheet of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) emergency department visits and hospital stays among Colorado residents, by county. It's the data behind the COPD dashboard on the Colorado Environmental Public Health Tracking site.
population: Colorado residents

name: Current asthma among adults by census tract, 2023
description: Estimated share of adults with current asthma in each Colorado census tract in 2023. The estimates are copied from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) PLACES dataset. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Adults

name: Diagnosed diabetes among adults by census tract, 2023
description: Estimated share of adults with diagnosed diabetes in each Colorado census tract in 2023. The estimates are copied from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) PLACES dataset. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Adults

name: Disability estimates, 2020–2024
description: Counts and percentages of people with a disability for each Colorado census tract, from the U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey (ACS) 2020–2024 estimates. It breaks disability down by age group and by type of difficulty: hearing, vision, thinking and memory, walking, self-care, and living independently. It's one of the layers of the CDPHE community health equity map. You can download the data or view it on a map. No longer updated.
population: Colorado residents

name: Drug overdose deaths involving prescription opioids or heroin by census tract, 2020–2024
description: Age-adjusted death rate per 100,000 people from drug poisoning or overdose involving prescription opioid painkillers or heroin, for each Colorado census tract from 2020 to 2024. The data come from CDPHE vital statistics. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents

name: Health eMoms
description: A former CDPHE online survey program that followed postpartum people in Colorado from shortly after birth to their child's third birthday. CDPHE sampled people each month from live birth certificates and invited them by mail; from 2018 to 2021, 2,400 people joined and completed up to six brief online surveys. Topics included breastfeeding, vaccinations, maternal mental health, social connection, maternity leave and family-friendly workplaces, child care, financial and resource insecurity, health care access, marijuana and other substance use, and oral health. Weighted results are published for the 2018, 2019, and 2020 birth cohorts, plus a COVID-19 survey sent to all cohorts in early 2021. The program ended in 2021 and was succeeded by the Baby & You Survey, so no new data will be added.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: Postpartum people with a Colorado live birth, through the child's third birthday

name: Healthcare-associated infection data
description: Data on infections people get while receiving health care, such as in hospitals, dialysis centers and nursing homes. CDPHE's healthcare-associated infections (HAI) program publishes reports, data pages and a dashboard. Record-level data are not available.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Patients in Colorado health care settings

name: Healthy Kids Colorado Survey
description: Colorado's most comprehensive survey of youth health and well-being. It is an anonymous, voluntary survey of a random sample of public middle and high school students, given every fall of odd-numbered years. Results are weighted to represent enrollment in Colorado public schools. Topics include mental health and suicide risk, substance use, nutrition, physical activity, bullying, sexual health, and protective factors such as support from caring adults and connection to school. CDPHE publishes statewide and regional results in the summer of even-numbered years.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Public middle and high school students (grades 6-12)

name: Heart attack data (download)
description: A downloadable spreadsheet of heart attack hospital stays among Colorado residents, by county. It's the data behind the heart attack dashboard on the Colorado Environmental Public Health Tracking site.
population: Colorado residents

name: Heart disease deaths by census tract, 2020–2024
description: Age-adjusted death rate per 100,000 people from heart disease, for each Colorado census tract from 2020 to 2024. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents

name: Heat-related illness data (download)
description: A downloadable spreadsheet of the data behind the heat-related illness dashboard: rates of heat-related illness per 10,000 health care visits in Colorado, by county, year and setting.
population: Colorado residents

name: Life expectancy by census tract, 2010–2015
description: Estimated life expectancy at birth for residents of each Colorado census tract, based on death records from 2010 to 2015. The estimates were published by the U.S. Small-Area Life Expectancy Estimates Project (USALEEP). They're older than most layers of the community health equity map. You can download the data or view it on a map.
population: Colorado residents

name: Low birth weight by census tract, 2020–2024
description: The share of single births (not twins or more) with low birth weight in each Colorado census tract from 2020 to 2024. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: Single live births to Colorado residents

name: Newborn Hearing Screening Program data
description: Data on hearing screening, diagnostic evaluation, and early intervention for babies born in Colorado, tracked up to age 3. Screening results come from the electronic birth certificate. Follow-up screening, audiology evaluation, and intervention data are entered by providers in the Health Information Data Systems (HIDS) Newborn Hearing application. The data track progress toward the EHDI 1-3-6 goals: screened by 1 month, evaluated by 3 months, and receiving intervention by 6 months. Values under 5 are suppressed. Data for 2025 and later are provisional and may change. Annual data appear in the Maternal and Child Health Dashboard and a yearly data overview.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
Access to and Linkage with Healthcare
population: Infants born in Colorado, birth to age 3

name: Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System
description: A CDC-funded surveillance system that tracks the behaviors and experiences of women before, during, and after pregnancy. Each month a stratified random sample of Colorado residents with a recent live birth is surveyed at 2-4 months postpartum by mail, phone, or web. Responses are linked to birth certificate data. Topics include preconception health, prenatal and postpartum care, insurance, breastfeeding, alcohol, tobacco, and marijuana use, mental health, maternal morbidity, and experiences of discrimination. About 1,100 people respond each year, and data are released every winter.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
Access to and Linkage with Healthcare
Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents ages 15+ with a recent live birth

name: Respiratory virus immunization data (download)
description: A downloadable version of the data behind the respiratory virus immunization dashboard. It shows how many Colorado residents have received seasonal flu, COVID-19 and other respiratory virus vaccines. The numbers come from the Colorado Immunization Information System (CIIS).
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Colorado residents in the immunization registry

name: State Unintentional Drug Overdose Reporting System
description: Detailed data on unintentional and undetermined-intent drug overdose deaths in Colorado. It combines death certificates, coroner and medical examiner reports, and toxicology reports to show when, where, and how overdose deaths happen and the circumstances around them. Data collection began with deaths in July 2019 and runs on a six-month cycle as part of CDC's Overdose Data to Action program. Findings are published in HealthWatch reports and the Colorado drug overdose dashboards. Data requests go to the Health Statistics office.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: All ages

name: Suicide deaths by census tract, 2020–2024
description: Age-adjusted suicide death rate per 100,000 people for each Colorado census tract from 2020 to 2024. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents

name: Teen births by census tract, 2020–2024
description: Birth rate among teens ages 15 to 17 in each Colorado census tract for 2020 to 2024: live births per 1,000 females in that age group. The data come from Colorado birth records and are updated every September. You can download the data or view it on a map.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: Females ages 15 to 17

name: Adult cannabis use, 2024
description: Shows how many Colorado adults use cannabis, how often, and how they use it, along with their views about it. The data come from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), a yearly phone survey of adults. Data are from 2024. Most views are statewide, and a geography tab shows six regions: Northwest, Northeast, Denver-Boulder, South Central, Southwest and Southeast. The data can't be downloaded from the dashboard. For other BRFSS topics, see the BRFSS summary tables.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Adults 18+

name: Asthma emergency department visits and hospitalizations, 2004–2025
description: Shows how often Colorado residents went to the emergency department (ED) or stayed in the hospital for asthma. Emergency department visits cover 2011 to 2025 and hospital stays cover 2004 to 2025. You can break it down by year and county. The data come from hospital discharge records and exclude federal facilities such as VA hospitals. The dashboard shows a data table but doesn't let you download; the data can be downloaded from the environmental tracking site.
population: Colorado residents

name: Birth defects, 2007–2016
description: Counts and crude rates of birth defect cases among Colorado births from the Colorado Health Information Dataset (CoHID). Data cover 2007 to 2016. Select a specific condition (such as anencephaly) and county to see cases over time and by maternal age, maternal race, maternal Hispanic origin, and infant sex. The data can't be downloaded.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: Infants born to Colorado residents

name: Cancer incidence, 2000–2020 (historical race categories)
description: Age-adjusted cancer incidence rates for Colorado residents from the Colorado Central Cancer Registry, published through the Colorado Health Information Dataset (CoHID). Select a cancer site, county, and years, and compare rates by sex, race, and Hispanic origin. Rates based on fewer than three cases are suppressed. Uses historical bridged (single) race categories with Hispanic origin.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents, all ages

name: Cancer incidence, 2000–2023 (excludes race)
description: Age-adjusted cancer incidence rates for Colorado residents from the Colorado Central Cancer Registry, published through the Colorado Health Information Dataset (CoHID). Select a cancer site, county, and years, and compare rates by sex. Rates based on fewer than three cases are suppressed. Race and Hispanic origin are not shown; see the companion dashboards for data by race.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents, all ages

name: Cancer incidence, 2020–2023 (includes race)
description: Age-adjusted cancer incidence rates for Colorado residents from the Colorado Central Cancer Registry, published through the Colorado Health Information Dataset (CoHID). Select a cancer site, county, and years, and compare rates by sex, race, and Hispanic origin. Rates based on fewer than three cases are suppressed. Uses the 2020 Census race categories (races alone and two or more races) with Hispanic origin.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents, all ages

name: Candida auris (C. auris) cases, 2019–2026
description: Shows cases of Candida auris (C. auris), a drug-resistant fungus that spreads in health care settings, in Colorado from 2019 to 2026. Cases are broken down by race and ethnicity, and mapped by county of residence and by county where the case was diagnosed. You can download the data from the dashboard.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Patients in Colorado health care settings

name: Cannabis exposures reported to the poison center, 2000–2025
description: Shows calls about cannabis exposures to Rocky Mountain Poison and Drug Safety, Colorado's poison center, from 2000 to 2025. Calls come from the public and from medical professionals. Results are statewide, by age group (5 and under, 6 to 12, 13 to 19, 20 to 29, and 30 and older). The data can't be downloaded.
population: People with a reported cannabis exposure

name: Cannabis use during pregnancy and breastfeeding, 2014–2023
description: Shows cannabis use before, during and after pregnancy, and while breastfeeding, among people who recently gave birth in Colorado. The data come from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) and cover 2014 to 2023, statewide. For other PRAMS topics, see the PRAMS summary tables.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: People with a recent live birth

name: Cannabis-related emergency department visits and hospital stays, 2004–2024
description: Shows emergency department visits and hospital stays in Colorado that include at least one cannabis-related billing code, from 2004 to 2024. Use the year slider to change years. Most views are statewide, and a geography tab shows six regions: Northwest, Northeast, Denver-Boulder, South Central, Southwest and Southeast. The data come from the Colorado Hospital Association and can be downloaded from the dashboard.
population: Patients at participating Colorado hospitals

name: Carbon monoxide poisoning emergency department visits, hospitalizations and deaths, 2000–2025
description: Shows carbon monoxide poisoning among Colorado residents: emergency department visits (2011 to 2025), hospital stays (2004 to 2025) and deaths (2000 to 2025). Emergency department and hospital data are shown by county as age-adjusted and age-specific rates, and can be filtered by year, sex, age group and whether the poisoning was fire-related. Death counts are shown by year and by type (fire, non-fire or undetermined). You can't download from the dashboard itself, but the data can be downloaded from the environmental tracking site.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents

name: CDPHE community health equity map, 2020–2024
description: An interactive map of Colorado census tracts that shows health conditions alongside social factors. Health layers include life expectancy, asthma, diabetes, drug overdose deaths, heart disease deaths, low birth weight, teen births and suicide. Social layers include population density, age, disability, education, employment, income and poverty, language, and race and ethnicity. Most layers cover 2020 to 2024, but some use other years (asthma and diabetes are from 2023, and life expectancy is from 2010 to 2015). Each layer names its own data source.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents

name: Child fatality prevention system (CFPS) dashboard, 2009–2020
description: Data from Colorado's Child Fatality Prevention System, which reviews all deaths of infants, children, and youth under age 18 that occur in Colorado. Topic pages cover suicide, sudden unexpected infant death, motor vehicle and other transportation, child maltreatment, firearms, drowning, homicide, and poisoning and overdose. Data cover 2009 to 2020. Each page shows counts, rates, and circumstances, with filters for year, demographics, and jurisdiction. The data can't be downloaded.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Children and youth ages 0-17

name: Childhood lead poisoning, 2007–2025
description: Shows blood lead testing among Colorado children from 2007 to 2025: the share of children tested and the number with a blood lead level of 3.5 micrograms per deciliter or higher. Choose a year and an age group (under 3, 3 to under 6, under 6, or under 19), and see statewide or county results. You can't download from the dashboard itself, but the data and a data dictionary are on the environmental tracking site.
population: Children and teens under 19 in Colorado

name: Colorado adult oral health dashboard, 2012–2024
description: Shows oral health among Colorado adults from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), for every other year from 2012 to 2024. Measures cover tooth loss, dental visits in the past year, dental insurance, delayed dental care, and how adults rate the health of their teeth. Results can be broken down by demographics (such as age, sex, race and ethnicity, income and urban or rural location), health care access, other health conditions, risk behaviors and social factors. Statewide results cover every survey year, and results for the 21 Health Statistics Regions combine 2020, 2022 and 2024. You can download the data.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Adults 18+

name: Colorado Basic Screening Survey dashboard, 2003–2023
description: Shows results of the Colorado Basic Screening Survey (BSS), in which kindergarten and third-grade students get a quick dental check at school. Results cover five school years from 2003–04 to 2022–23 and include measures such as tooth decay, broken down by race and ethnicity, the share of students at the school who get free or reduced-price lunch, and urban or rural location. Results are statewide only. Survey methods changed over time, so use caution when comparing years. You can download the data as a spreadsheet.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Kindergarten and third-grade students

name: Colorado drug-related emergency department and hospital use, 2016–2025
description: Colorado Hospital Association data on emergency department visits and hospital stays from 2016 to 2025. One section covers nonfatal drug overdoses and the other covers substance use disorder diagnoses. Both can be shown by county of residence, Health Statistics Region or opioid settlement region. You can export the tables shown, but not the underlying data.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents, all ages

name: Colorado health indicators (CHI) dashboard
description: A set of public health indicators at the county, regional, and state level that together describe the overall health of a community. Indicators are grouped into social and institutional equity, living conditions, health behaviors, disease and injury, and mortality. The dashboard supports Colorado's Health Assessment and Planning System (CHAPS) and includes data source information sheets and archived data downloads. The dashboard doesn't say which years the data cover. Data source sheets that give a date mostly say 2020.
population: All ages

name: Colorado HIV/AIDS prevention, care and treatment strategic plan (COHAS) dashboard, 2022–2026
description: Tracks Colorado's HIV prevention, care and treatment plan (COHAS) for 2022 to 2026. It has sections on pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), HIV testing, syringe access services, people newly diagnosed with HIV, HIV care and treatment through the Ryan White program, and providers and community. Maps show results for eight regions of the state: Northwest, Central North, Northeast, the Denver Transitional Grant Area (TGA), Central West, Southwest, Central South and Southeast. You can view each section for priority populations, including Black, Native American and Hispanic or Latino people, men who have sex with men, women, rural residents, transgender and nonbinary people, and Spanish speakers. The page says it updates every quarter, but it shows data only from early 2022 through the end of 2024.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
Access to and Linkage with Healthcare
population: Colorado residents, with views for priority populations

name: Colorado maternal and child health dashboard, 2016–2024
description: Brings together key maternal, infant, child, and youth health indicators from state and federal sources, including PRAMS, the Baby & You survey, the National Survey of Children's Health, the Maternal Mortality Prevention Program, and the Newborn Hearing Screening Program. The landing page shows the latest state-level data. Indicator tabs add trends, demographic breakdowns, and county or regional data where available, with downloadable spreadsheets. Years vary by indicator: maternal mortality covers 2016 to 2023, most perinatal indicators 2023 to 2024, child and youth indicators from 2020–21 to 2023–24, and newborn hearing screening 2020 to 2023.
topics: Maternal, Child, Adolescent, and Family Health
population: Pregnant people, infants, children, and youth

name: Colorado measles vaccination data, 2024–2026
description: Shows measles vaccination in Colorado from the Colorado Immunization Information System (CIIS). The coverage tab shows the share of people in each county who have had at least one dose or more, by age group (from 6 months to adults 19 and older). The administration tab shows doses given each month in 2024, 2025 and 2026, by county. Small counts are hidden, and the dashboard updates every Sunday.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Colorado residents in the immunization registry

name: Colorado motor vehicle crash problem identification dashboard, 2021–2025
description: Describes motor vehicle crashes in Colorado so that transportation, law enforcement, local agencies, and prevention partners can find traffic safety problems and target prevention. Views cover injuries and crashes by year and county, contributing factors, at-fault driver demographics, toxicology and alcohol impairment in fatal crashes, and safety behaviors of occupants and nonmotorists. A map overlays fatality and serious injury rates with EnviroScreen scores.
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: All ages

name: Colorado population estimates
description: Colorado population estimates from the Colorado Health Information Dataset (CoHID), produced with the State Demography Office and used as denominators for vital statistics rates. View total population by county, sex, and age group, with one view for 2000–2019 using bridged (single) race categories and one for 2020–2025 using the 2020 Census race categories.
population: Colorado residents, all ages

name: Colorado reportable disease data
description: Shows yearly case counts and rates, statewide or by county, for diseases that must be reported to the state. The data behind it are also available to download. STIs, hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis and lead are tracked separately.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Colorado residents

name: Colorado tuberculosis (TB) data dashboard, 1992–2025

Other tabs show cases by demographics and by birthplace (born in the U.S., born outside the U.S. or unknown) for 2016 to 2025, and case rates by county for 2016 to 2025. You can download the data from the dashboard. It can take a minute to load.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: People diagnosed with TB in Colorado

name: Colorado WIC data dashboard
description: Shows current WIC enrollment in Colorado, broken down by race and ethnicity, age, infant and child sex, the mother's education, language spoken, and participation in programs such as SNAP. topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado residents, all ages

Data come from several sources, including the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS), the Healthy Kids Colorado Survey and the American Community Survey, and years vary by measure, from 2015 to 2021. name: Viral respiratory diseases report, 2024–2026

The data can't be downloaded from the dashboard, but related datasets are on the CDPHE open data portal, and older data files and past flu season reports are linked from the page.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control

name: VISION chronic disease dashboard, 2012–2024
description: Shows the burden of chronic disease in Colorado, organized around CDPHE's 1-3-4-50 model. Health factors include alcohol use, cancer prevention and screening, mental health, nutrition, oral health access, physical activity, and tobacco use. Health outcomes include cardiovascular health, diabetes, older adult health, oral health, respiratory illness, suicide, and weight status. Each indicator has trend charts, tables, maps, and downloadable data, and the dashboard highlights how place and structural factors shape health disparities. Data cover 2012 to 2024, statewide, with breakdowns by adult age group (18–24 up to 65 and older).
topics: Chronic Disease, Injury Prevention, and Behavioral Health Promotion
population: Colorado adults

Other tabs show this season's cases by county and demographics, a map of past cases, and tables of cases by county and year, and by neurologic or non-neurologic illness, back to 2003, when the virus became reportable. Counts change as public health staff investigate new cases. The data can't be downloaded.
topics: Communicable Disease Prevention, Investigation and Control
population: Colorado residents
